hero.headline: Trump to decide on Iran deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz and eliminate uranium stockpile
hero.body:
President Trump issued an aggressive ultimatum to Iran on Sunday, demanding the country reopen the Strait of Hormuz by Tuesday night at 8 p.m. Eastern Time or face military strikes on power plants and bridges. Trump posted on Truth Social that "Tuesday will be Power Plant Day, and Bridge Day, all wrapped up in one, in Iran. There will be nothing like it!!!"

The threat came amid a broader backdrop of conflict in the region. A US F-15E fighter jet crashed in southwest Iran, and American special forces rescued a second crew member after a two-day search. Iran released images of aircraft wreckage but did not deny that US forces had recovered the downed pilot.

Trump has extended deadlines multiple times for Iran to reopen the strait, which serves as a critical shipping chokepoint for roughly one-fifth of the world's oil supply. The latest threat triggered immediate market reaction, with crude oil prices rising sharply on Monday. West Texas Intermediate climbed 1.86 percent to more than $112 per barrel, while Brent crude climbed above $110.

Despite the hostile rhetoric, Trump separately suggested negotiations were ongoing. He told Fox News there was a "good chance" of reaching an agreement with Iran on Monday. "If they don't make a deal and fast, I'm considering blowing everything up and taking over the oil," he said.

Iran's parliament speaker, Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf, responded to the threats by warning that Trump's "reckless moves" would cause the region to "burn." He stated that the United States would not gain anything through what he characterized as war crimes and called for respecting Iranian rights instead.

Trump's inflammatory language drew sharp criticism from Democratic leaders. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer posted that "the President of the United States is ranting like an unhinged madman on social media" and accused him of threatening possible war crimes while alienating allies.

International law experts raised serious concerns about the threatened attacks. Oona Hathaway, a professor of international law at Yale University, stated that if the threatened strikes on civilian infrastructure were carried out, they would constitute war crimes. Under the Geneva Conventions, civilian objects receive protection during conflict, and attacking them for bargaining leverage violates international law.

The conflict has already caused extensive damage across the region. Iranian authorities report that about 81,000 civilian sites have been damaged, including 61,000 homes, 19,000 commercial sites, 275 medical centers, and nearly 500 schools. Both sides have continued striking economic infrastructure, with Iran attacking petrochemical facilities in Bahrain and Kuwait over the weekend.

cards.headline: Exxon Warns Oil Inventories Could Reach Dangerously Low Levels
cards.teaser: The energy supermajor cautioned that oil prices could hit $160 within weeks as inventories decline.
cards.body:
A major oil company has cautioned that oil inventories will decline to critically low levels in the coming weeks, potentially driving prices sharply upward. The supermajor suggested that oil prices could reach $160 per barrel as global supplies tighten.

The oil market has few solutions to address the emerging supply shortage. Industry analysts emphasize that crude oil production cannot be rapidly scaled up to meet demand, noting the fundamental constraint that physical supply constraints cannot be solved through financial or technological shortcuts alone.

cards.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes, threatening NASA lunar mission timeline
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a static fire test at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida on Thursday evening, creating a significant setback for the company and NASA's lunar exploration plans. The massive fireball destroyed the launchpad at Kennedy Space Center seconds after the test began at 9pm ET, with the explosion's glow visible over 115 miles away in Fort Pierce and shockwaves felt across Florida's space coast.

The incident occurred just days after NASA announced that Blue Origin had won a contract to launch the first of three uncrewed lunar missions planned for this year to begin construction of a $20 billion moon base. NASA's Artemis program aims to return astronauts to the Moon for the first time since 1972, with missions scheduled for 2027 and 2028. Blue Origin is developing the Blue Moon lander that will transport astronauts from the Orion capsule to the lunar surface, making this explosion a direct threat to the agency's timeline.

Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos confirmed in a statement that all employees were safe and uninjured. He described it as "a very rough day" and said the company was working to determine the root cause. "It's too early to know but we're already working to find it. We'll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying," Bezos wrote.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman announced that a full evaluation of mission timelines would be conducted following the explosion. He acknowledged that "spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult." The agency committed to working with Blue Origin to support a thorough investigation and assess impacts to the Artemis and Moon Base programs.

This explosion represents the latest in a series of setbacks for Blue Origin as it competes with SpaceX for NASA contracts. Last month, a payload from New Glenn's third flight ended up in the wrong orbit, leading the Federal Administration to temporarily ground the rocket. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared it to return to flight.

The launchpad remained engulfed in flames for more than two hours after the explosion. Emergency officials reported no threat from fumes or other hazards. The incident triggered widespread attention on social media, with residents from nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach reporting shaking homes and posting photos of the orange fireball visible from the beach.

NASA's plans to establish a sustained human presence on the Moon now depend on a swift investigation and resolution of whatever technical issues caused the explosion. The space industry has faced multiple setbacks in recent years as companies develop new launch systems, with comprehensive reviews typically requiring months or sometimes years before operations resume.

cards.headline: FBI arrests former CIA official with $40 million in gold bars in home
cards.teaser: A former senior CIA official faces charges after investigators found $40 million worth of gold bars inside his home.
cards.body:
David Rush, a former senior CIA official, remains in custody in Virginia after being accused of stealing 303 gold bars and over $2 million in foreign currency from the agency. According to an FBI affidavit, Rush allegedly took the bullion bars—each weighing approximately 2.2 pounds—along with the cash from his government office.

Federal investigators discovered the gold bars hidden at Rush's residence. His initial court appearance was postponed to the following week as the case proceeds.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Allows Companies to Avoid Taxes Through Foreign Havens
cards.teaser: US companies have avoided at least $40 billion in taxes since early 2025 using schemes in Malta, Bermuda, and Cyprus.
cards.body:
The Trump administration cleared the way for companies to use tax avoidance schemes in foreign jurisdictions including Malta, Bermuda, and Cyprus. US companies have skirted at least $40 billion in taxes since the beginning of 2025 through these arrangements.

The policy change enables corporations to shift profits to low-tax or no-tax jurisdictions, reducing their US tax obligations. Malta and Cyprus, both European Union member states, along with Bermuda, a British overseas territory, are among the primary locations used for these tax structures.

cards.headline: Justice Department launches criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors opened a criminal probe targeting E. Jean Carroll and a nonprofit connected to Reid Hoffman that funded her lawsuits against Trump.
cards.body:
The Justice Department started a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, who won civil judgments against President Trump in defamation cases. The probe also targets a Reid Hoffman nonprofit organization that provided financial backing for Carroll's legal claims.

The top federal prosecutor in Chicago denied the investigation exists, disputing media reports about the probe. The inquiry has created complications for Senate Republicans as they navigate the political implications of investigating a Trump accuser.

hero.headline: Russian Drone Strikes Romanian Apartment Building, Injuring Two
hero.body:
A Russian drone hit a residential apartment building in Romania, injuring two civilians, Romanian officials said. The strike marks the first time civilians have been injured in Romania from drones related to the nearby war in Ukraine.

Romania is a member of NATO, and the security alliance issued a statement condemning what it called Russian recklessness. The incident sharply escalated tensions between NATO and Moscow.

Romania announced it will hold an emergency meeting following the strike. The apartment building was located near the Ukrainian border, an area that has seen a growing number of drone incursions as the conflict continues.

Drones from the war in Ukraine have repeatedly crossed into Romanian airspace in recent months, but this marks the first incident to cause injuries to civilians on Romanian soil. The strike raises questions about the security of NATO member states bordering the conflict zone.

The NATO statement did not specify what actions the alliance might take in response to the incident. Russia has not publicly commented on the strike. Romania has been providing humanitarian support to Ukraine since the war began, though it has not been directly involved in combat operations.

The two injured civilians were in the apartment building at the time of impact. The extent of their injuries was not disclosed by Romanian authorities. The strike caused damage to the residential structure, though officials did not provide details about the scale of destruction.

The incident comes as Ukraine has been expanding its drone operations against Russian positions. Multiple reports indicate Ukrainian forces have been using new mid-range strike drones to target areas previously considered safe for Russian operations. These operations have been particularly active following what sources described as a difficult winter for Ukrainian forces.

cards.headline: Trump Says Decision Coming Soon on Iran Proposal
cards.teaser: The president said Iran must agree to his demanded concessions and that he was prepared to lift the naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
President Trump said he is meeting with advisers to make a final determination on an Iran deal after U.S. and Iranian officials confirmed they had agreed on a deal framework. Trump stated that Iran must accept his demanded concessions and indicated he was prepared to lift the naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route for global oil supplies.

The announcement represents the latest step in ongoing negotiations between the two countries over the strategically important waterway.

cards.headline: U.S. Designates Brazilian Drug Gangs as Terrorist Groups
cards.teaser: The Trump administration labeled Brazil's two largest drug gangs as terrorist organizations following advocacy by the Bolsonaro family.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced that the United States has designated Brazil's two largest criminal organizations—the First Capital Command (PCC) and the Red Command—as foreign terrorist organizations. The move places these gangs on the same legal standing as international terror groups and may trigger U.S. sanctions and enforcement measures.

The designation is seen as a political setback for Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who opposed the measure. The announcement is being viewed as a boost for Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula's far-right challenger in Brazil's upcoming October presidential election.

cards.headline: European Union to Release Billions to Hungary After Electoral Defeat for Orban
cards.teaser: The EU is set to release 16 billion euros previously withheld as Hungary moves to implement anti-corruption and rule of law reforms.
cards.body:
The European Union will release more than €16 billion to Hungary that was frozen during Viktor Orbán's tenure. EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described the decision as reflecting "winds of change" following the election of Prime Minister Péter Magyar last month. Magyar called the move a "historic breakthrough" for the country.

The decision coincides with other policy shifts in Hungary. Police have announced they will permit next month's Pride parade in Budapest to proceed, reversing last year's government-ordered ban on the event. These developments signal a significant departure from the previous government's approach to democratic freedoms and rule of law.

cards.headline: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty to Aiding Suicides by Selling Toxic Chemical Online
cards.teaser: Kenneth Law admitted to charges relating to Canadian victims after allegedly being linked to nearly 150 deaths worldwide.
cards.body:
Kenneth Law, a Canadian man, pleaded guilty to 14 counts of assisting suicide after mailing "suicide packets" containing lethal chemicals to more than 100 people across dozens of countries, including Canada, the UK, the US, Italy, Australia and New Zealand. He appeared in court in Newmarket, Ontario, where prosecutors withdrew 14 murder charges in exchange for his guilty plea.

Law's case has been linked to nearly 150 deaths worldwide, including 79 in Britain. While he admitted to charges relating to Canadian victims, he will not face justice in the UK over the British deaths. Families of victims have called for him to be charged in Britain as well. Sentencing is scheduled for September.

cards.headline: Former Shaolin Temple Abbot Sentenced to 24 Years for Corruption
cards.teaser: Shi Yongxin, the ex-head monk of China's famous kung fu temple, was jailed for embezzlement and bribery.
cards.body:
Shi Yongxin, the former abbot of China's Shaolin Temple, was sentenced to 24 years in prison for embezzlement and bribery, according to state media reports. The Shaolin Temple is internationally known for its association with kung fu and martial arts traditions.

The corruption case against the former head monk represents a high-profile conviction in China's ongoing anti-corruption efforts. Shi Yongxin had led one of China's most famous religious and cultural institutions before the charges were brought against him.

cards.headline: British Museum Cancels Jewish Cultural Event Over Disruption Threat
cards.teaser: The postponement comes during a period of rising racial and religious crimes in Britain and growing unease among London's Jewish community.
cards.body:
The British Museum postponed a Jewish cultural event, citing the threat of disruption. The cancellation comes as Britain has seen a rise in racial and religious crimes and as some members of London's Jewish community report a growing sense of unease.

The museum did not provide specific details about the nature of the disruption threat. The decision to cancel the event reflects broader security concerns for Jewish community activities in the British capital.

cards.headline: Federal judge blocks Trump administration's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: A US judge halted the Justice Department from operating a $1.8 billion fund established by the Trump administration.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Virginia issued a temporary block on Friday preventing the Trump administration from transferring money into a $1.8 billion fund. US District Judge Leonie Brinkema barred the Justice Department from taking any further steps to create or operate the fund while legal challenges to the program proceed.

The administration established the fund to address what it characterized as weaponization of government agencies. The judge's order aims to prevent any irreversible disbursement of funds while the legal case continues.

cards.headline: Justice Department launches criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors opened a criminal probe targeting E. Jean Carroll and a nonprofit connected to Reid Hoffman that funded her lawsuits against Trump.
cards.body:
The Justice Department started a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, who won civil judgments against President Trump in defamation cases. The probe also targets a Reid Hoffman nonprofit organization that provided financial backing for Carroll's legal claims.

cards.headline: Attorney General Bondi defends Justice Department handling of Epstein files to Congress
cards.teaser: Pam Bondi testified about the Justice Department's management of files related to Jeffrey Epstein in a long-sought appearance before lawmakers.
cards.body:
During closed-door testimony, former Attorney General Pam Bondi acknowledged that redaction errors occurred in the release of Epstein documents. She defended the Justice Department's overall handling of the sensitive files, characterizing it as reflecting an "unprecedented commitment to transparency" in the case.

Bondi, who was ousted as attorney general in April, faced congressional questioning about the department's management of the Epstein materials. Democratic lawmakers noted that she declined to answer questions regarding Trump's involvement in the Epstein files.

cards.headline: Kenyan court blocks US plan to quarantine American Ebola patients in Africa
cards.teaser: A court in Kenya halted a US proposal to establish an Ebola quarantine facility in the country following public protests.
cards.body:
A Kenyan court blocked the United States from opening an Ebola quarantine camp on Kenyan soil. The decision came after protests against the proposed facility, which would have housed Americans who contract Ebola while abroad.

US officials now say Americans who get Ebola will be sent to Europe for treatment instead of being brought back to the United States. The proposed facility sparked backlash both in Kenya and among Americans who questioned the decision to exclude infected citizens from domestic treatment.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra leads California governor's race in new polling
cards.teaser: A second poll shows Xavier Becerra ahead in California's gubernatorial race, with Steve Hilton and Tom Steyer trailing.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra has taken the lead in California's governor's race according to a Berkeley IGS poll. Steve Hilton and Tom Steyer ranked second and third in the survey of likely voters.

The poll results come as California heads toward its 2026 primary election. Multiple surveys now show Becerra with an advantage over other candidates seeking to lead the state.

hero.headline: Maintenance Train Fire at Penn Station Injures Five, Disrupts Rail Service
hero.body:
A maintenance train caught fire at Penn Station, injuring five people and disrupting rail service across multiple commuter lines. The fire suspended service for NJ Transit and Amtrak, while Long Island Rail Road service has been restored.

The blaze occurred at the major transit hub in New York, which serves as a critical junction for regional rail networks. Photos from the scene showed a fireball inside the station. The fire involved a maintenance train rather than a passenger service vehicle.

Five individuals sustained injuries in the incident. The nature and severity of the injuries have not been specified in available reports.

NJ Transit and Amtrak services remained suspended following the fire. The disruption affected commuters traveling between New York and New Jersey, as well as those using Amtrak's Northeast Corridor services. LIRR, which also operates out of Penn Station, restored its service after the initial disruption.

MTA officials provided an update on the fire and its impact on station operations. The cause of the fire has not been disclosed.

Penn Station serves hundreds of thousands of commuters daily and functions as one of the busiest transportation hubs in North America. The station handles traffic for three separate rail operators: Amtrak, NJ Transit, and the Long Island Rail Road.

The timing of service restoration for the affected lines has not been announced. Commuters were advised to seek alternative transportation or expect significant delays.

Maintenance trains are used for track work, repairs, and other infrastructure upkeep within the rail system. They typically operate during off-peak hours or in designated work zones to minimize interference with passenger service.

cards.headline: Dell Stock Surges 33 Percent on AI Server Demand
cards.teaser: Dell shares jumped sharply as demand for artificial intelligence servers and price increases drove strong quarterly results.
cards.body:
Dell shares soared 33 percent following strong quarterly results driven by robust demand for AI servers and price increases. The gain marked the company's best single-day performance in two years.

The surge significantly boosted founder Michael Dell's personal wealth by $34 billion, elevating his position among the world's wealthiest individuals.

cards.headline: SEC Moves to Eliminate Climate Change Disclosure Rule
cards.teaser: The Securities and Exchange Commission proposed killing a regulation that would have required publicly traded companies to disclose climate risks.
cards.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission proposed eliminating its climate change disclosure rule, which would have required publicly traded companies to reveal significant climate-related financial risks in their mandatory filings.

The regulation had not yet been implemented. Eliminating it would remove investor protections by allowing companies to withhold information about how climate change could affect their business and finances.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Drop on Signs of US-Iran Agreement
cards.teaser: Oil prices fell as investors assessed tentative signs of a pact to extend a cease-fire between the US and Iran.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell sharply on Thursday following reports of a potential breakthrough in US-Iran ceasefire negotiations. Brent crude futures, the global benchmark, declined 1.3% to around $92 per barrel as investors responded to signs of a possible agreement.

The price drop reflects broader market optimism about reducing tensions in the region. Brent crude has fallen 19% since the end of April, marking its steepest monthly decline since 2020. Stock markets rallied alongside the declining oil prices as traders assessed the implications of a potential peace deal.

cards.headline: Anthropic Valued at $900 Billion, Surpassing OpenAI
cards.teaser: The artificial intelligence company reached a $900 billion valuation, exceeding OpenAI's worth.
cards.body:
Anthropic has raised $65 billion in funding, bringing its valuation to $965 billion and making it the world's most valuable AI startup. The company, which develops the Claude chatbot, has surpassed OpenAI in valuation during what appears to be a final private fundraising round before a potential IPO.

The company's rapid ascent reflects its transformation from a smaller player in the AI sector to an industry leader. Enterprise adoption of Anthropic's products has accelerated significantly, particularly following the release of powerful coding assistants. The funding round underscores continued investor confidence in the artificial intelligence market.

cards.headline: South Korean chip startup raises $135 million betting on memory bottleneck in AI
cards.teaser: XCENA secured funding based on the theory that artificial intelligence systems face greater constraints from memory access than computing power.
cards.body:
South Korean chip startup XCENA secured $135 million in funding based on the theory that memory represents AI's primary performance constraint, rather than raw computing power. The investment signals growing recognition that traditional approaches to AI chip design may have overlooked a critical limitation.

XCENA's strategy diverges from mainstream chip development by prioritizing data access and storage efficiency over computational throughput. This alternative approach reflects broader industry interest in reimagining AI hardware architecture to address what the startup sees as the real bottleneck holding back AI system performance.

cards.headline: China launches new crew to space station with year-long mission planned
cards.teaser: A fresh crew of astronauts launched to China's Tiangong space station, with one member scheduled to remain in orbit for 12 months.
cards.body:
China has launched its Shenzhou-23 mission, lifting off from the Jiuquan launch centre with three astronauts aboard a Long March 2-F rocket bound for the Tiangong space station. For the first time, one astronaut will spend a full year in orbit.

The extended mission represents a key milestone in China's lunar ambitions, as the country works toward landing humans on the moon by 2030. Year-long spaceflights provide essential data on how the human body adapts to prolonged weightlessness, knowledge that will inform future deep space exploration efforts.

cards.headline: Cognition CEO says AI coding tool not designed to replace programmers
cards.teaser: Scott Wu, whose company built Devin, said the AI coding agent aims to assist rather than supplant human developers.
cards.body:
Cognition's CEO Scott Wu has emphasized that Devin, the company's AI coding agent, is not designed to replace human programmers. Wu, a respected coder himself, made the clarification as the industry debates AI's role in software development.

Devin is considered the first and most successful AI coding agent to date. As companies increasingly explore how AI tools can enhance development workflows, Wu's statement underscores the company's vision of augmenting rather than eliminating the need for human engineers.

cards.headline: Sennheiser releases Momentum 5 wireless headphones with improved noise cancellation
cards.teaser: The new headphones feature upgraded active noise cancellation technology and a battery users can replace themselves.
cards.body:
Sennheiser launched its Momentum 5 wireless headphones with enhanced active noise cancellation and audio performance. The headphones include a replaceable battery, a feature that allows users to extend the product's lifespan by swapping out the power source when it degrades.

Reviews highlighted the improvements to both sound quality and noise cancellation compared to previous models. The replaceable battery addresses a common complaint about wireless headphones, where built-in batteries eventually fail and force consumers to replace the entire device.

cards.headline: Acer launches $699 laptop with Intel processors to compete with MacBook
cards.teaser: The Swift Air 14 includes Intel chips and 8GB of RAM at a price point below Apple's entry-level offerings.
cards.body:
Acer introduced the Swift Air 14, a 14-inch laptop starting at $699 designed to compete with Apple's MacBook offerings. The device uses Intel's Core Series 3 "Wildcat Lake" processors—either Core 5 or Core 7 models, both with six cores—and includes 8GB of RAM in its base configuration. The laptop is available in green.

The launch reflects the Windows PC industry's efforts to challenge Apple's laptop dominance with more affordable alternatives.

cards.headline: Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 leak suggests three models including Classic version
cards.teaser: Product codenames indicate Samsung may release three variants of its next smartwatch, potentially bringing back the Classic design.
cards.body:
Leaked codenames indicate Samsung is preparing three distinct Galaxy Watch 9 models for release, including a return of the Classic variant. The multiple models reflect Samsung's strategy to serve different customer preferences across various price points.

The leak also suggests Samsung will adopt a feature from Google's wearable technology for the new watches.

hero.headline: Jose Mourinho returns to Real Madrid as head coach
hero.body:
Jose Mourinho has signed a three-year contract to become Real Madrid head coach for the second time, marking his return to the Spanish club 13 years after his first spell ended.

The 63-year-old Portuguese manager previously led Real Madrid from 2010 to 2013. During that period, he won La Liga in the 2011-12 season and claimed the Copa del Rey in 2011. He also guided the club to three Champions League semifinals, though he never reached the final during his time at the Bernabeu.

Real Madrid was his preferred choice for the role, with talks having taken place over the past period to bring him back to the club. His appointment comes after he was managing Benfica, where he had been since September. The club was reluctant to lose him but needed to establish contingency plans for a potential departure.

Mourinho's experience at the highest level of European football made him an attractive candidate for Real Madrid's leadership. Since leaving the Spanish capital over a decade ago, he has managed several top clubs including Chelsea, Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur, and Roma. His career achievements include winning league titles in four different countries: Portugal, England, Italy, and Spain. He has also won two Champions League titles, both secured with Porto and Inter Milan.

The appointment reunites Mourinho with a club where he experienced both significant success and notable controversy. His first tenure saw tensions with certain players and criticism of his defensive approach to the game. However, his consistent track record of winning major trophies and handling pressure at elite clubs convinced Real Madrid to bring him back.

Real Madrid has been seeking managerial stability following recent changes in the dugout. The club was recently named the most valuable club in world football according to a new valuation, with Barcelona overtaking Manchester United to claim second place. This reinforces the status of Real Madrid as one of football's biggest institutions.

With this appointment, Mourinho will take charge of a squad containing some of the world's best players. He will be expected to compete immediately for both the Champions League and La Liga title, restoring the club's dominance in Spanish and European football. His tactical acumen and winning mentality at top clubs will be crucial as Real Madrid aims to rebuild its competitive edge at the highest levels of the game.

The three-year deal reflects the club's confidence in Mourinho's ability to deliver success and stability during a period when establishing consistency in management was a priority for the Spanish giants.

cards.headline: French Open to take action against player for remarks about female umpire
cards.teaser: Adolfo Daniel Vallejo criticized a female umpire after his second-round match at the French Open.
cards.body:
The French Open announced disciplinary action against Adolfo Daniel Vallejo following sexist remarks about his second-round match official. The Paraguayan player criticized Brazilian umpire Ana Carvalho, claiming a man should have officiated the match instead, allegedly because she couldn't control the crowd's support for his opponent, French teenager Moïse Kouamé.

Vallejo lost the match 6-3, 7-5, 3-6, 2-6, 7-6 (8) after nearly five hours on Court Suzanne Lenglen. His comments drew swift condemnation from tournament organizers, players, and tennis officials, reigniting debate over gender equality in professional tennis officiating.

cards.headline: Knicks center Mitchell Robinson injures pinkie finger before NBA Finals
cards.teaser: New York Knicks center Mitchell Robinson suffered a pinkie finger injury ahead of the NBA Finals.
cards.body:
Mitchell Robinson underwent surgery on a broken pinkie finger just before the Knicks are set to compete in the NBA Finals. The center's injury raises questions about his availability for the championship series.

Robinson reportedly plans to play in the NBA Finals despite the injury and subsequent surgery. The Knicks have not provided a definitive timeline for his return, but sources indicate the team remains hopeful he will be able to participate in at least some of the finals games.

cards.headline: Players call for sponsorship board removal after French Open injury
cards.teaser: Katie Boulter wants on-court sponsorship boards removed after Zeynep Sonmez was injured tripping over one.
cards.body:
British player Katie Boulter has called for the French Open to remove on-court sponsorship boards following an injury to Turkish player Zeynep Sonmez. Sonmez retired from her match after tripping over one of the boards during play at Roland Garros.

The incident has raised safety concerns among players at the tournament, highlighting worries about court conditions and player welfare at major tennis events.

cards.headline: Champions League final not free to air despite pressure
cards.teaser: TNT Sports will not make the Arsenal-PSG Champions League final available without a subscription.
cards.body:
Fans will need a TNT Sports subscription to watch the Champions League final between Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain, after the broadcaster decided against making the match free to air. This decision comes despite pressure from supporters to provide wider access to the major occasion.

The final represents a significant moment for Arsenal as they compete for European glory. The paywall decision has disappointed many who hoped the broadcaster would make the match available to all viewers.

cards.headline: Teenage cricketer Sooryavanshi scores 96 after recovering from head blow
cards.teaser: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hit 96 off 47 balls in the Indian Premier League second qualifier.
cards.body:
Teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi delivered a brilliant performance in the Indian Premier League's second qualifier, scoring 96 runs off just 47 balls. The impressive innings demonstrated his aggressive batting ability on cricket's biggest stage.

Sooryavanshi's performance was particularly noteworthy as it came after he had recovered from a head injury, showcasing his resilience and determination as a young player.

cards.headline: New Zealand beats Ireland by innings and 79 runs in first Test
cards.teaser: New Zealand wrapped up victory on day three of their one-off Test match against Ireland.
cards.body:
New Zealand completed an emphatic victory over Ireland on day three of their one-off Test at Stormont, winning by an innings and 79 runs. The result was straightforward, with Ireland captain Andy Balbirnie acknowledging that his side were not performing at the same level as their opponents.

Nathan Smith was instrumental in the victory, taking five wickets in just 29 balls to dismantle Ireland's batting. The bowler's performance proved decisive in securing New Zealand's comprehensive win in this historic first Test between the two nations.

hero.headline: Filmmaker Jorge Gutierrez Exits Amazon AI Series After Backlash
hero.body:
Filmmaker Jorge Gutierrez announced he will no longer produce an AI-generated animated series for Amazon Prime Video. The decision came after public backlash following this week's announcement of his involvement in the project.

Gutierrez apologized to those he upset with the project. Amazon MGM Studios had planned to fund the series as part of a new initiative supporting AI-generated entertainment projects.

The filmmaker made the announcement publicly, stating he had decided to drop out of the Amazon-backed production. The project was part of Prime Video's broader push into AI-generated content.

Amazon's initiative represents one of the first major streaming platform efforts to fund entertainment created using artificial intelligence tools. The company had not disclosed how many other projects were in development under the program.

Gutierrez is known for his work in animation, though specific details about the planned AI series were not released before his withdrawal. The backlash centered on the use of AI technology in content creation, a topic that has generated significant debate in the entertainment industry.

The entertainment industry has faced growing tensions over AI-generated content. Writers, animators, and other creative professionals have raised concerns about AI tools potentially replacing human creators or using their work without compensation.

Amazon MGM Studios has not commented on whether the initiative will continue or if other creators remain attached to AI projects under the program. The company also has not responded to questions about how Gutierrez's departure might affect its AI content strategy.

The announcement marks a significant setback for Amazon's AI entertainment push. Major streaming platforms have been exploring ways to incorporate AI technology into content production, but have faced resistance from creative communities and labor unions representing industry workers.

cards.headline: Paramount Acquires Florence Pugh Film in Cannes Bidding War
cards.teaser: Paramount Pictures secured North American and select international distribution rights to The Midnight Library following competitive bidding at the Cannes film market.
cards.body:
Paramount Pictures secured North American and select international distribution rights to The Midnight Library following a competitive bidding process at the Cannes film market. Florence Pugh stars in and produces the adaptation, with Garth Davis directing.

Studiocanal, the production and distribution division of Canal+ Group, will handle distribution across the U.K., France, and Germany. The deal marks a significant acquisition for Paramount at the international film marketplace.

cards.headline: Michelle Pfeiffer Emerges as Emmy Contender With Two Series
cards.teaser: Michelle Pfeiffer became an Emmy contender this year after two series she stars in premiered around the same time.
cards.body:
Michelle Pfeiffer found herself in an unexpected position as an Emmy overachiever after serendipitous timing led her Paramount+ drama The Madison and Apple TV+ comedy Margos Got Money Troubles to debut near each other. She also recently appeared in a Prime Video project.

The actress did not plan to have multiple projects compete in the same awards season. The timing resulted from production schedules aligning in ways she had not anticipated when signing on to the different series.

cards.headline: HBO Max Series Half Man Reveals Emmy Strategy
cards.teaser: The Richard Gadd-created HBO Max miniseries submitted 21 official Emmy entries, with lead actors splitting into different categories.
cards.body:
HBO Max's limited series "Half Man," created by Richard Gadd, has unveiled its Emmy submissions strategy following the conclusion of its six-episode run. The show submitted 21 entries across various Emmy categories.

Jamie Bell, who portrays the lead character Niall Kennedy, will compete in the lead actor category. Richard Gadd, the series creator, is pursuing a nomination in the supporting actor category rather than lead.

cards.headline: YouTube Horror Series Backrooms Adapted Into Hollywood Film
cards.teaser: YouTuber Kane Parsons' internet series about endless yellow corridors has been turned into a feature film.
cards.body:
An internet meme featuring endless yellow corridors has made the leap to the big screen. The Backrooms concept originated online and inspired a YouTube horror series by Kane Parsons, which has now been adapted into a theatrical film.

The film stars Chiwetel Ejiofor as Clark, an architect-turned-furniture store owner who discovers a portal to a mysterious realm of backrooms in his showroom basement. The project exemplifies a growing trend of YouTube horror creators transitioning to major studio productions, joining filmmakers behind recent hits like Talk to Me and Iron Lung.

cards.headline: Broadway Musical Galileo Releases Space-Themed Video
cards.teaser: Producers of the upcoming Broadway musical Galileo sent a copy of The Starry Messenger to the edge of space for a promotional video.
cards.body:
Producers Amanda Lipitz, Henry Tisch, and Jordan Roth released a video promoting their upcoming musical Galileo. The video shows a copy of Galileo's book The Starry Messenger being sent to the edge of space, with astrophysicist Neil deGrasse Tyson providing narration.

Lipitz confirmed the video was not AI-generated. The promotional effort ties the historical scientist's work to modern space exploration ahead of the musical's Broadway opening.

cards.headline: Director Adam Shankman Says Stop That Train Revives Old Comedy Genre
cards.teaser: The comedy film opening June 12 features RuPaul as a fictional U.S. president dealing with a runaway high-speed train.
cards.body:
Stop That Train hits theaters June 12, featuring RuPaul as Madame President. The film centers on the Glamazonian Express, a high-speed train struck by lightning during a severe storm that sends it careening toward disaster.

Director Adam Shankman positions the movie as a return to an older style of comedy—one focused on silliness. While managing the crisis, the fictional president grapples with concerns about her approval ratings, allowing the film to blend absurdist humor with high-stakes scenarios.

hero.headline: Trump approval rating falls to 34 percent, lowest recorded in YouGov survey
hero.body:
President Trump's job approval rating has dropped to 34 percent in the latest YouGov/The Economist poll, representing the lowest point recorded in the survey across both of his terms in office.

The rating falls below any approval rating that former President Biden achieved during his entire presidency, according to YouGov data. The survey, which tracks presidential approval on a weekly basis, has now established a new low benchmark for Trump's standing with the American public.

The decline occurs as Trump faces multiple challenges affecting his political position. According to recent polling, his approval has been sliding for months. By October 2025, nine months into his second term, his rating had already fallen to 42 percent, matching the level Biden reached more than three years into his presidency, according to researchers at the University of Massachusetts Lowell.

Several factors appear to be contributing to the falling support. Voters have expressed significant disapproval of Trump's economic policies. An estimated 64 percent of voters disapprove of his handling of the economy, traditionally considered one of Trump's strongest issues. A majority of voters have also criticized his management of the cost of living, immigration, and the Israel-Palestine conflict.

Economic hardship has become a central concern for Americans. The nationwide average fuel price now stands at almost 4.52 dollars per gallon, up from 3.18 dollars a year ago. Among independent voters, 47 percent say his policies have personally hurt them, compared with 41 percent in the previous year.

The administration's approach to deportations has also affected his support. According to the researchers, confrontations during deportation operations, in which two U.S. citizens were killed by federal agents, undermined his backing. The fallout from the decision to join Israel in striking Iran, along with the resulting oil crisis, appears to have accelerated the decline.

Recent polling shows that most American voters believe the decision to go to war with Iran was wrong. Nearly two-thirds of voters said entering the conflict had been the wrong choice, and fewer than one in four Americans said the war had been worth the costs.

When asked about the economic hardship inflicted on Americans, Trump said: "I don't think about Americans' financial situation."

The YouGov/The Economist poll surveys a representative sample of American adults on a weekly basis and tracks public opinion across multiple political issues. Presidential approval ratings are closely watched as indicators of political strength and public sentiment heading into elections.

cards.headline: Russian drone crashes in Romania, Putin adviser warns European Union
cards.teaser: A Russian drone crashed in Romania, prompting a warning from a top Kremlin official that Europe has entered the war with Russia.
cards.body:
A Russian drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania on Friday during an overnight attack on Ukraine, injuring two people, according to Romanian authorities. NATO confirmed the drone was of Russian origin, though Moscow initially denied responsibility. Putin subsequently requested that the wreckage be handed over to Russia for an independent investigation.

The incident has intensified tensions on NATO's eastern flank. Czech President Petr Pavel has called on the alliance to "show its teeth" in response to Russia's repeated provocations, proposing decisive measures including cutting off Russian internet access, severing banks from global financial systems, and shooting down aircraft that violate allied airspace.

cards.headline: Immigration slowdown affects U.S. economy as population growth stalls
cards.teaser: President Trump's immigration policies have caused one of the sharpest slowdowns in U.S. population growth in decades, with economists warning of lasting damage.
cards.body:
The Trump administration's immigration crackdown is producing one of the steepest declines in U.S. population growth in modern history. Economists have begun calculating the economic effects, with some warning the damage could persist well into the second half of the century.

The immediate impact appears in monthly employment figures, as the economy generates fewer jobs. The policy-driven immigration reversal has few modern parallels. Over time, reduced immigration could create a productivity drag that lasts for decades, according to economic analyses.

cards.headline: Rep. Frederica Wilson announces retirement after 16 years in Congress
cards.teaser: The Florida Democrat will not seek reelection, becoming the 30th House Democrat from the current Congress who will not return.
cards.body:
Rep. Frederica Wilson announced Friday that she will not seek reelection, ending her 16-year tenure in Congress. The South Florida Democrat made the announcement as she joins a growing wave of House Democrats departing after the 119th Congress.

Wilson becomes the 30th House Democrat from the current Congress who will not be joining the 120th Congress in the upcoming term.

cards.headline: Sen. Cornyn shares scorpion fable after Trump endorses primary opponent
cards.teaser: The Texas senator posted the story of a frog and scorpion after President Trump backed Ken Paxton, who won the GOP primary.
cards.body:
Sen. John Cornyn shared the fable of the frog and the scorpion on social media after President Trump endorsed state Attorney General Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate GOP primary. Paxton won decisively, ending Cornyn's reelection campaign.

Cornyn had compiled a voting record that aligned with Trump 99.3 percent of the time during his Senate tenure. The cryptic post of the classic fable, in which a scorpion stings a frog carrying it across a river despite knowing both will drown, came after Trump's endorsement proved decisive in the primary race.

cards.headline: Former Defense Secretary says U.S.-Iran deal would ease Strait of Hormuz tensions
cards.teaser: Mark Esper said a memorandum of understanding between the two countries would reduce pressure over energy prices and the strategic waterway.
cards.body:
Former Defense Secretary Mark Esper said a memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran would relieve pressure on both countries regarding the Strait of Hormuz. The agreement is intended as a step toward an eventual peace deal between the two nations.

Esper described the deal as primarily addressing tensions over the strategic waterway, through which a significant portion of global oil supplies pass. He suggested the agreement would also help ease concerns about energy prices for both countries.

cards.headline: Speaker Johnson's longtime chief of staff to leave office in June
cards.teaser: Hayden Haynes, who has worked with Mike Johnson since his first congressional campaign in 2016, will depart as chief of staff.
cards.body:
Speaker Mike Johnson's longtime chief of staff, Hayden Haynes, will depart his position in early June. Haynes has been one of Johnson's most enduring aides, beginning as his campaign manager when Johnson first ran for Congress in 2016.

Haynes transitioned to chief of staff when Johnson entered office and continued in the role as Johnson advanced to Speaker. The departure marks the conclusion of a partnership spanning Johnson's entire political career, from his initial campaign through his rise to leadership.
